question: From 8 to 12 June 2026 in Vienna, an Erasmus+ training course was held on ‘queer youth and allies: building inclusive youth work’, for 30 youth workers to discuss ‘intersectionality’ and how to create ‘more inclusive spaces for queer young people’. 1.
What specific objectives and measurable outcomes did the Commission aim to achieve by funding this course, and to what extent are these in line with the core objectives of EU youth policy?
What was the total cost of this course, including the contributions made by Erasmus+ and the European Solidarity Corps towards accommodation, meals, travel and organisation?

Which organisations and individuals (please provide names) from which countries of origin took part in the course as participants, trainers or cooperation partners (including OeAD, SALTO, WienXtra and Q:WIR), or were involved in shaping its content?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) The Erasmus+ programme seeks to promote equal opportunities, inclusiveness, diversity and fairness across all its actions.

The training course referred by the Honourable Member was organised by the Austrian National Agency for Erasmus+ and the SALTO (Support, Advanced, Learning and Training Opportunities) resource centre for Inclusion and Diversity in Education and Training.

It brought together youth workers, educators, and trainers to learn and co-create more inclusive, diverse and supportive environments for lesbian, gay, bisexual, trans, non-binary, intersex and queer (LGBTIQ+) young people.

The training course is in line with the inclusion priority set by the Erasmus+ Regulation1 and the objectives of the EU Youth Strategy 2019-20272, in particular aiming to ensure equal opportunities, access to rights and non-discrimination for all young people regardless of gender identity or sexual orientation.

This is aligned with the EU fundamental values of equality and non-discrimination, enshrined in the Treaties, the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union3 and the European Pillar of Social Rights, as well as the commitments taken by the Commission in the LGBTIQ equality strategy 2020-2025, as renewed in the LGBTIQ+ equality strategy 2026-20304.

The description of the course, with a total budget of EUR 65 308.36, its aims and objectives are provided on the website of SALTO inclusion and diversity5. The personal data of participants is protected under the Regulation (EU) 2018/1725 on the protection of personal data by the EU institutions6.
